# Resolve.

> Resolve. is the independent software and data engineering consultancy of Johan Schuijt: LLM extraction and search, interfaces for working with data, and full-stack product development, mostly for organizations doing public-interest work — journalism, accountability and open data.

Johan Schuijt is an autodidact software and data engineer with fifteen-plus years of experience. Current work: project lead of EveryPolitician at OpenSanctions, structuring politicians' data for investigators and the accountability sector through PoliLoom. Previously full-stack developer at Follow the Money. Resolve. is registered as Resolve Services OÜ in Estonia (e-residency), VAT EE102834268. Works remotely, Europe-focused, global clients welcome.

Contact: johan@resolve.works, +31 651 952 461.

## Pages

- [Homepage](https://resolve.works/): Services, way of working, current work, selected experience and FAQ
- [Articles](https://resolve.works/articles/): Essays on tools, data and the open web

## Articles

- [Everything in its place](https://resolve.works/articles/everything-in-its-place/): Syncthing, KeePass, Restic and GrapheneOS — an open, self-controlled setup that syncs files and secrets across every device
- [Pi is a really nice agent](https://resolve.works/articles/pi-is-a-really-nice-agent/): How a small-core, extensible coding agent was shaped around one person's work: focused extensions, delegated contexts, deterministic code intelligence and open-weight models
- [The tool is not the author](https://resolve.works/articles/the-tool-is-not-the-author/): Photography, auto-tune and machine translation settled it long ago — the human who directs the tool owns the output; LLMs are no different
- [AI agents are human too](https://resolve.works/articles/ai-agents-are-human-too/): AI agents are being blocked from the web they read on our behalf; the reasons are economic, not technical, and the blocking doesn't even work
